data.long_meaning: The name Sokin is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sok', which means 'Lord'. The suffix 'in' signifies 'the Earth'. Thus, Sokin is the name of the Lord of the Earth. The name Sokin carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sokin usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This concept is deeply rooted in Hindu tradition and is expressed through various rituals, practices, and mythologies.

historical_references.reference:
Sokin was a king who ruled the Vatsa kingdom in north India during the 3rd century BCE. He is known for his military conquests and is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a friend and ally of the Pandavas.
Reference: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, Section XLIV, Verse 11.
Time period: 3rd century BCE
Context: Ancient Indian history, Hinduism
